item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03340","case1_error":"Subtracts only Ryan's quarter-share, omitting Chris's withdrawal.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 63 after correctly stating the total plates and subtraction formula.","reason":"The first visibly omits a withdrawal; the second shows correct formulas but an unsupported number, without revealing its calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03341","case1_error":"Omits the four cookies Ted eats when calculating cookies remaining.","case2_error":"Adds both original batches to the remaining brownies, counting the first batch twice.","reason":"Omitting a required consumption differs from double-counting an original batch.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03342","case1_error":"Divides days by remaining words instead of words by days.","case2_error":"Assigns the entire workload to each worker and sums their times instead of optimizing simultaneous work.","reason":"The first reverses a rate ratio; the second duplicates work and incorrectly combines concurrent completion times.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03343","case1_error":"Uses remaining water as water lost to calculate jumps, then unjustifiably subtracts that jump count from itself.","case2_error":"Divides revenue remaining after wages by employee count instead of dividing the wage allocation.","reason":"The first constructs erroneous threshold and subtraction relations; the second calculates a different monetary quantity despite correctly finding total wages.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03344","case1_error":"Counts Reece's ladder only once, omitting his 15 climbs.","case2_error":"Leading answer marker says 14, but the derivation correctly calculates the combined size as 21.","reason":"The first omits a repetition factor; the second has only an answer-marker conflict, requiring an uncertain judgment.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
